Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 471 of 2016
 Smt. Vishnubai And Others
 Versus
 Said And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.3.
 With
 Misc. Appeal No. 466 of 2016
 Sushil Kumar
 Versus
 Said And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.3.
 Order

The present appeals have been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being
aggrieved by the award dated 17.11.2015 passed in Claim Case Nos. 57/2014 and 59/2014.

The
M.A.No. 471/20
16 has been filed by the legal representatives of the deceased Govindram and M.A.No. 466/2016 has been filed by the injured Sushil Kumar Jain/claimant.
The challenge is made to the dismissal of the claim petitions on the ground that the involvement of the vehicle was not found proved.

2. The facts relevant for the purpose of the present case are that as per the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35680 2 MA-471-2016 story in the claim petition, on 01.03.2014 Govindram as rider and Sushil Kumar Jain as pillion rider were going on a motor cycle from Jaora to Ratlam for participating in counselling of the Education Department.
When they reached near Namli Railway Bridge, truck bearing registration No. MP 43 G 1188 came from behind and dashed into their motor cycle.

The wheel of the truck crushed the head of Govindram because of which he died on the spot and Sushil Kumar Jain sustained injuries and became unconscious due to trauma suffered by him at the spot itself.
The persons who were standing by, called the Ambulance 108 and took both persons to the District Hospital Ratlam.
For the death of Govindram and for the injuries to Sushil, separate claim petitions were filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The Tribunal after recording Smt. Vishnubai vs Said on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193173240/
1 evidence concluded that the claimants were not able to prove that the insured vehicle was involved in the accident.

1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, both the claim petitions were dismissed by the impugned award.
3. The Tribunal while considering the issue number 1 regarding involvement of the vehicle recorded its findings from para 12 to 22.

The Tribunal particularly found the statement of Heeralal unreliable for the reason that he did not inform to any officer of the police about the incident whereas there were several occasions when he crossed the police station or the patrolling police while he was on the way to Brahmano Ka Bas in Ratlam.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that infact, the Tribunal wrongly considered the fact that while Dehati Nalishi was registered on the information of Sushil Kumar Jain after about 2 hours of the accident, he was still not knowing the number of the vehicle.
He submits that infact this is completely in sink with the version given by the different witnesses of the claimants before the Tribunal.

He points out that because of the trauma, Sushil Kumar Jain got unconscious and remained as such for a period of six minutes but before that he NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35680 3 MA-471-2016 had given the number of Vinod Kumar Jain his brother to Heeralal who was present at the spot of accident.
The said Heeralal informed Vinod Kumar Jain about the occurrence of the accident.

He further points out that in the statement of Vinod Kumar Jain recorded by police under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C., Vinod has not stated that he was informed about the number of vehicle which caused accident.
In fact, his version is that Heeralal called him at about 10:45 and informed that his brother got injured in an accident.
Thereafter, he rushed to the District Hospital Ratlam.
He thus submits that in the entire story, it has not come that either Sushil Kumar Jain or Vinod Kumar Jain were aware about the number of the vehicle.

It is only after about 5 days when the said persons called back to the number from where information of the accident had come i.e. the number of Heeralal, then only they came to know about the number of the offending vehicle.
He points out that the FIR was also registered on the same day.
As such, the version of both the witnesses i.e. Sushil Kumar Jain and Heeralal are completely in sink with each other.

Learned counsel further submits that infraction on the part of Heeralal that he did not inform the police cannot be a ground for refusal for grant of compensation to the appellants in the claim petition and can also not be a ground to disbelieve the evidence which was brought before the Tribunal as the same is consistent and prompt.
He thus prays for allowing of both the appeals and setting aside the conclusion of the Claims Tribunal with respect to not finding the involvement of the insured vehicle proved.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / insurance company points out that Heeralal in his deposition before the Tribunal particularly in para 6 of his cross-examination has though initially stated that he did not inform the number of vehicle to anybody but later on said that he had informed about the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35680 4 MA-471-2016 same to Vinod Kumar Jain.
However, Vinod Kumar Jain was not examined by the claimants before the Tribunal.

He further points out that Vinod Kumar Jain after getting information about accident rushed to the hospital and he was with Sushil Kumar Jain when the Dehati Nalishi was recorded by the Police on the information of Sushil Kumar Jain.

Once Heeralal had informed the number of the vehicle and Vinod Kumar Jain was with Sushil Kumar Jain when Dehati Nalishi was being recorded,
it was natural that he should have informed the number of the vehicle to the police which had not Smt. Vishnubai vs Said on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193173240/
2 been done.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He thus submits that the entire story of the claimants is not only suspicious but is fabricated.
Hence, the Tribunal has correctly discarded the Claim petition and no interference is warranted.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the record.

7. The accident occurred on 01.03.2014 and Dehati Nalishi was registered on 01.03.2014 itself at around 12:30 in the afternoon after which the FIR was registered on the same day in the police station.
Both of them were registered against an unknown vehicle.

The contention of learned counsel for the appellant that it is only natural that the Dehati Nalishi and FIR was registered against an unknown vehicle for the reason that the injured Sushil Kumar Jain and his brother Vinod Kumar Jain were not aware about the number of the offending vehicle which is clear from the statement of Sushil Kumar Jain and Section 161 statement of Vinod Kumar Jain.
They have stated that they were aware about the occurrence of accident but have no where stated that they were informed about the vehicle number.

In the statement of Heeralal (AW-2), it has clearly come in para 2 that after few days of accident he received a phone call from the same number on which he had informed about the accident and the number of the offending vehicle was asked on phone he informed the number and thereafter he went to police station where he informed about the number of offending vehicle again.

As such, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35680 5 MA-471-2016 the number of the offending vehicle came to light only after registration of Dehati Nalishi and FIR as per the statement of eye-witness.

The statement of eye-witness is totally in line with the statement of the injured Sushil Kumar Jain who has stated in examination before the Tribunal that he become unconscious after the accident but before that he gave the phone number to a person who was standing there for informing about the accident to his brother.
He also submits that few days later a call was made to the number from where the information of accident was given and thereafter they came to know about the number of the vehicle.

Thus, both the statement of Heeralal and Sushil Kumar Jain are consistent with each other considering the fact that the FIR of the accident was lodged on the same day and also the fact that statement of eye-witness Heeralal has not got washed out in cross-examination except the fact that he has admitted the fact that he did not inform the police.
There is nothing to disbelieve his version.
It is not the case of the insurance company that the owner of the vehicle is related to the deceased or the injured person in any manner.
It is also not the case of the insurance company that the eye-witness was related in any manner with the claimants.

This Court has also gone through the report of the investigator of the insurance company in which though, the investigator has recorded that he contacted two eye-witnesses i.e. Heeralal (AW-2) & Anokhilal and recorded that both of them have denied that the insured vehicle was involved in the accident however, he has not recorded their statements.

The report is clearly an evasive report which has plainly denied the occurrence of accident without any efforts to record the evidence of even a single person though the investigator claims that he has contacted all the related persons i.e. injured, legal heirs of the deceased, two eye- witness, the owner,
the driver, etc.
8.

From the conclusions drawn by the Tribunal, it is apparent that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35680 6 MA-471-2016 Tribunal has stressed upon the fact that Sushil Kumar Jain-the injured failed to disclose the number of the offending vehicle when the Dehati Nalishi was Smt. Vishnubai vs Said on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193173240/
3 recorded after two hours of the accident and even in the FIR when it was recorded on the same day.

While observing thus, the Tribunal has completely remained oblivious of the fact that the said injured i.e. Sushil Kumar Jain himself has stated that he was not aware about the number of the vehicle and this was never the story of the injured that he was aware about the number of the vehicle at any stage during the course of the day when both the documents were recorded.

In fact he clearly stated in his evidence before the Tribunal that he came to know about the number of vehicle only after few days when his brother called back the person who informed about the accident.

Also considering the fact that the police has conducted investigation and final report under Section 173 of Cr.P.C. has been filed observing involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident, as such there is clear perversity in the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

9. Considering the peculiar facts of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the matter deserves to be remanded back to the Claims Tribunal so as to decide the issue of involvement of the vehicle afresh.
At this stage, learned counsel for parties pray that they may be given liberty to lead further evidence in support and rebuttal of the occurrence of the accident.

10. Considering the aforesaid, the matter is remanded back to the Claims Tribunal for deciding the issue of involvement of the vehicle afresh after giving opportunity of leading evidence to the parties,
if so expressed.
11.
Parties are directed to appear before the Claims Tribunal on 28.01.2026 and on such further dates as may be directed by the Tribunal in this regard.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35680 7 MA-471-2016
With the aforesaid, the appeals stand disposed of.
Registry is directed to immediately send back the record of the Claims Tribunal.
Let a copy of this order be kept in the connected M.A.No.466/2016.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE vidya Smt. Vishnubai vs Said on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193173240/
